name: browser/extract-table
title: Table to CSV
summary: Pull a table or list from a web page into a CSV file and check the rows.
when: Use when the user wants the rows of a web table or list as a spreadsheet they can open.
steps: Call browser with action open, the url and selector table so the result is the table as Markdown, not the whole page.
If the selector returns nothing, call browse_page on the url and find the table or list in the readable text.
Keep every column the page shows and write the header line first, in the same order as the page.
Call write_file with a path ending in .csv and content that has one header line and one line per row, commas quoted.
Call analyze_table with only the path to read the row count, the column names and the cells that are empty.
Compare that row count with the number of rows you counted on the page and call fetch_page to recheck any gap.
If the page needs a login or blocks reading, say so plainly and save the part you read, marked as partial.
Report the file path, the row count and the columns, and call open_path when the user wants to see the file.
next: The final answer must give the CSV file path, the number of data rows written and the column names, noting any partial read.
